h1: Sita Beach Resort Koh Lipe — the quiet end of Pattaya Beach, still walkable to the buzz
intro: Pattaya Beach is Koh Lipe's liveliest main beach, but Sita Beach Resort sits at the quieter far end — same white sand and clear water, without falling asleep to beach bars all night. It's a 4-star resort on roughly 12 acres of beachfront, with 61 rooms across seven types, from hillside garden-view rooms to pool villas and honeymoon suites. What guests bring up most is the sea-view infinity pool and the breakfast buffet. From approx. THB 2,800/night. Scored 9.0 from 247 reviews.

body.html: Sita Beach Resort sits at the quiet far end of Pattaya Beach, the main beach on the west side of Koh Lipe. The upside of this spot is that you get Pattaya Beach's white sand and clear water in full, and you can walk along the shore to Walking Street — the island's hub of restaurants and dive shops — in about 10–15 minutes, yet at night it's quieter than the central stretch where the bars run late. The resort spreads across roughly 12 acres of beachfront, so it doesn't pack rooms in tightly like the smaller places on the island.

There are 61 rooms across seven types. They range from hillside garden-view rooms and pool-view Superiors to honeymoon suites and a two-bedroom pool villa. Rooms are done in a contemporary Thai style with a balcony, bathtub, minibar and an LCD TV. Most reviews praise the rooms as spacious and clean, with cold, strong AC and good water pressure — something not every resort on Koh Lipe manages consistently.
"Coming down in the morning to sit by the infinity pool and watch the Andaman change colour as the sun comes up — then a few steps to white sand. It felt worth choosing this end of the beach."

The thing guests talk about most is the two pools, with an infinity pool whose edge runs out toward the sea line — a photo spot everyone stops at. Add the calm, clean private beach in front of the resort, perfect for lounging all day. There's a spa for a relaxing massage, and a dive desk that easily arranges snorkelling and diving trips to the islands around — Koh Lipe is the gateway to the Tarutao archipelago.

On food, the breakfast buffet draws the most praise in reviews — varied choices, kept topped up, which on an island where everything arrives by boat is no small thing. The resort's beachfront restaurant is a fine spot for dinner to the sound of the waves, and if you want a change, walkable Walking Street has plenty of seafood and international places to choose from.

Honestly, the thing to accept is that the resort is built up a slope, and the upper garden-view rooms mean climbing several flights of steps. If walking is difficult or your bags are heavy, ask for a lower-zone room near the pool and beach. A few reviewers also note that some buildings and furniture feel a little aged and due for renovation, hot water isn't always reliable in some rooms, and the hillside rooms see mosquitoes in the evening. The cancellation policy is fairly strict too, so read the terms before you book.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: if you want the most convenient spot, ask for a lower-zone room near the pool and beachfront first — it cuts the stair-climbing and keeps you close to the water. For getting to the island, ferries and speedboats run mainly from Pak Bara pier (frequent in high season, Nov–Apr); the resort offers transfers from the boat drop-off to the beach. In high season rooms fill fast and rates climb noticeably, so book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Sita Beach Resort Koh Lipe

faq.q: Where is Sita Beach Resort on Koh Lipe?
faq.a: It sits at the quiet far end of Pattaya Beach, the main beach on the west side of Koh Lipe. You get Pattaya Beach's white sand and clear water in full, but it's quieter at night than the central stretch. You can walk along the shore to Walking Street — the island's hub of restaurants and dive shops — in about 10–15 minutes.

faq.q: How much does Sita Beach Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 2,800/night for a hillside Superior Garden View. From there you can step up to a Superior Pool View (40–50 sqm), a Superior Honeymoon Suite (60–66 sqm), and a Two Bedrooms Pool Villa (86 sqm) for families. There are seven room types in all. High-season rates rise noticeably — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Sita Beach Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples and families who want to be right on Pattaya Beach but away from the nighttime bar noise. There's a sea-view infinity pool, a calm private beach and a praised breakfast buffet — and you can still walk to Walking Street when you want food or a dive shop.

faq.q: Is there a lot of uphill walking, and is there a lift?
faq.a: The resort is built up a slope, and the upper garden-view rooms mean climbing several flights of steps. If walking is difficult or your bags are heavy, ask for a lower-zone room near the pool and beach when you book. Lower-zone rooms have easy access to the pool and the water.

faq.q: How do you get to Koh Lipe?
faq.a: Ferries and speedboats to Koh Lipe run mainly from Pak Bara pier in Satun, taking about 1.5 hours. They're frequent in high season (November–April). Koh Lipe has no deep pier, so boats anchor offshore and a longtail brings you in to the beach. The resort offers transfers from the boat drop-off to the beach.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and is cancellation flexible?
faq.a: In high season (November–April) book 1–2 months ahead, as rooms fill fast and rates climb noticeably. The cancellation policy here is fairly strict, so choose a Free Cancellation rate first if your plans aren't firm, then compare prices across a few platforms.
